chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the water which nothing can pollute. He said: A kurr. I said: And what is the kurr? He said: Three spans by three spans.

key_terms.أَشْبَار: plural of shibr — the span, measured from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger when the hand is fully open; approximately 22-25 cm
key_terms.الكُرّ: kurr — a unit of water volume in Islamic law; water of this quantity or more cannot be rendered impure by contact with najasa
key_terms.يُنَجِّسُهُ: to render impure/pollute (ritual sense, not merely physical); from najasah, ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: What is the kurr in Islamic law and how is it measured?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) establishes the jurisprudential definition of the kurr — the minimum volume of water that is not rendered impure by contact with a najis (ritually impure) substance. The Imam defines it as a cube of three hand-spans (ashbar) per side, which classical jurists calculated to approximately 377 liters. This ruling is foundational to the chapter on ritual purity (tahara) and water classification in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Ibn Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the water which nothing can pollute. Heasws said: ‘A Kurr’. I said, ‘And what is the Kurr?’ Heasws said: ‘Three open palm’s width by three open palm’s width’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqiy from ibn Sinan from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir who has said the following: “

I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the water which does not become unclean by anything. He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is one Kur.’ I then asked, ‘How much is one Kur?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is three shibr by three shibr in size.’”
